label: early original-phase step (t=1-3) on c/n/u/w/j/z/f/v-type token after a 3/p/l/2/i prefix
predicate: (t >= 1) & (t <= 3) & isin(in_tok, [tok("c"), tok("n"), tok("u"), tok("w"), tok("j"), tok("z"), tok("f"), tok("v"), tok("e"), tok("r"), tok("s"), tok("3")]) & seen([tok("3"), tok("p"), tok("l"), tok("2"), tok("i")])
explanation: About 81% of activation mass is in the original phase, mostly at t=1-3 (t=2 alone holds 40%). It never fires at t=0 and almost never on the delimiter or at orig_idx >= 5. Which tokens are involved matters: it prefers current inputs c (5x lift), n, u, w, j, z, f, v, and earlier inputs 3 (prev_tok lift 9.5x), p, l, 2, i. The strongest activations are on c right after 3 at the start of the sequence (e.g. "3 c", "p 3 c"); steps after a leading 3 or p are next. The remaining ~19% of mass is in the copy phase at recall_idx 2-4. It is weak there and only partly mirrors the original-phase pattern. The predicate gets mass recall ~0.63 but precision only ~0.2. Most early steps with these tokens stay inactive, so the gate depends on a token-combination code that a simple predicate does not capture. Magnitude rises with a 3 directly before the current token and with c as the current token.
